question: Which of the following types of patterns was followed in Mohenjodaro town planning?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Grid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The town planning of **Mohenjodaro**, one of the main sites of the **Indus Valley Civilization (IVC)**, followed a well-planned **grid pattern**.
 
• In a grid pattern, streets and lanes are arranged in straight lines, often intersecting at right angles to form a network of **rectangular blocks**.
 
• The streets in Mohenjodaro were aligned in a **north-south and east-west direction**, creating an organized layout.
 
• The grid layout also allowed for effective **drainage systems** and proper urban management, which was a hallmark of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• Each block in the grid contained houses, public buildings, and other structures, with a focus on functionality and uniformity.
 
• The advanced planning of Mohenjodaro reflects the importance of **urban planning and civil engineering** during the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• This pattern was unique for its time and is considered an early example of **planned urbanization**.
 
• The city’s layout demonstrates the existence of a governing authority that prioritized **hygiene, resource management, and organized settlements**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Circular**__

 __
 
• **Circular town planning** is generally observed in settlements that revolve around a central point such as a **temple, fort, or marketplace**.
 
• It was not a feature of the **Indus Valley Civilization** but is observed in certain ancient cities like those in **Mesopotamia**.
 
 
 
• **Rectangular**__
 __
 
• While the term "rectangular" may seem similar to the grid system, it primarily refers to the layout of individual buildings or structures rather than the entire town.
 
• Mohenjodaro’s streets and town planning were more organized in a **grid system** rather than just rectangular layouts.
 
 
 
• **Cylindrical**__
 
 
• A **cylindrical pattern** is not relevant to urban planning and does not describe any known ancient city layouts.
 
• This term is more applicable to **architectural forms or objects**, such as columns or storage vessels, rather than town planning.
